turns.text: boss quick one before my shift starts. county approved my health permit for commissary food, im taping the printout on my stall banner. what else am i supposed to have posted at a market stall

Congrats on the approval! Rules vary by county, so confirm with your county environmental health office or check your permit paperwork. Typical requirements for a market food stall:

- Permit displayed where customers and inspectors can see it (your banner works, at eye level)
- Handwashing setup: water with a spigot, soap, paper towels, and a catch bucket
- Food handler cards for anyone handling food, available on request
- Food kept covered and off the ground, with hot items held hot and cold items held cold. A thermometer on hand is a good idea
- Any required allergen or labeling info, depending on the county
- Your commissary name or address on file, since some counties want it available

The permit approval letter often lists the conditions. Is there anything in it you're unsure about?

ok actually i take cards now too, card reader on my phone under the business account. do card sales need any extra signs or notices. also paolo and i just changed the split to 70/30, he keeps instagram and market setup. who should be listed on the permit and signs lol

Card sales usually don't need a special posted notice. A few small things help though:

- Post your prices clearly, and note "cards accepted" and any minimum or surcharge. If you add a card fee, it generally has to be disclosed up front
- Your card reader app will email receipts, so mention that option at the stall
- Sales tax rules are a separate question. Ask your state tax agency whether you need a seller's permit

For names, the permit lists whoever the county issued it to, the person or business that applied. Signs just need to match that. Your split with Paolo is a private agreement between the two of you. It doesn't change who's on the permit, though if he'll be working the stall, he'd need his own food handler card. For ownership or liability, it's worth putting the 70/30 arrangement in writing. Who applied for the permit?

just me. ok last thing, i have my friday 5-9 block at the commissary tonight and ill be rolling alone again. paolo bailed on prep again, last week i rolled 200 by myself till midnight and my hands were wrecked. any hand stretch tips 🥢

Good, with the permit in your name the paperwork is simple. For your hands, since you'll be rolling repetitively for four hours:

- Warm up first by running warm water over your hands and doing a few gentle wrist circles
- Take a 60-second break every 30-40 minutes
- Wrist stretch: arm out, palm up, gently pull your fingers back with the other hand for 15-20 seconds. Then repeat with palm down
- Finger spread: open your hand wide, then make a loose fist. Do 10 reps
- Thumb stretch: gently pull the thumb back and across the palm for 15 seconds
- Switch grip and posture now and then, and keep your work surface at a comfortable height so your shoulders stay relaxed
- Do the same stretches again after you finish

If you get numbness or sharp pain, stop and rest. Do you want a short checklist for tonight's block?
